heading: Area law and PEPS approximation for gapped two-dimensional ground states
lede: Two manuscripts posted on September 24, 2026 claim proofs of two long-open statements about gapped quantum spin systems on the square lattice, assuming only that the full Hamiltonian has a spectral gap. This page follows the Lean formalization of both proofs.
description: Hourly progress of the Lean formalization of the two-dimensional area law and polynomial PEPS approximation.
label: openai-math

repos.name: TNLean
repos.description: Tensor-network theory in Lean 4: the fundamental theorem of matrix product states, canonical forms, parent Hamiltonians, matrix-product density operators, projected entangled pair states and local circuits.

repos.name: QICLean
repos.description: Quantum information and channels in Lean 4, following Wolf's Quantum Channels & Operations: channel representations, Kadison–Schwarz theory, quantum Perron–Frobenius and spectral theory, GKSL semigroups and entropy.

routes.heading: How the area law is proved
routes.intro: The proof shows that a piece of A shares almost no information with anything beyond a thin collar around it, then cuts A into regions whose entropies cancel. Each stage gives the physical idea, the results it needs, and the state of the formalization.

stages.title: A first bound below volume
stages.physics: The global gap limits how much the eigenvalues of a region's reduced state fluctuate on a logarithmic scale: reweighting the state by ρ−u/2 on a block costs energy only along the cut. The proof then optimizes a staircase of positive filters on nested rectangles, the norm {{tn:al-filter-norm}}, and bounds it from above and below; comparing the two bounds discounts the conditional entropy.
stages.delivers: A box of side r far from the cut has S ≤ C r1+e₀ with e₀ < 1. The volume bound would be r².
stages.caption: Entropy bounds for a box of side r on log–log axes, where each exponent becomes a slope. The volume bound has slope 2, this stage gives slope 1 + e₀ (drawn at e₀ = ½), and the area law is the dashed slope 1 that the later stages reach.

diagrams.caption: Proof of Lemma lem:tail. Reweighting a state Ψ by F = ρ−u/2 on a block B and tracing out the rest (the joined leg) gives σ = ρ1−u/M(u). Only terms crossing the cut feel F, so by the gap the tilted vector stays close to Ψ, which pins the fluctuations of −log pj.

Section 2: the norm N = ‖Lm⋯L1Ω‖ of a staircase of positive filters Lj on nested regions Xj ⊃ X (drawn for m = 2; Tj are the shells). Bounding −2 log N from above and below gives the discount on S(X | buffer).

stages.title: Make the Hamiltonian local and positive
stages.physics: Lieb–Robinson bounds in the lattice's own graph distance and a smooth spectral filter with stretched-exponentially decaying Fourier tails rewrite the Hamiltonian as a sum of positive local pieces ki. Each piece annihilates the ground state, {{tn:al-kill}}, and is supported on a ball up to a stretched-exponential tail.
stages.delivers: Positive operators that each annihilate Ω and have rapidly decaying spatial tails, and whose sum has a global gap.
stages.caption: Left: the spectrum of H as a rug, with the isolated ground energy and the gap. The filter vanishes at E₀ and is flat above the gap, so each piece annihilates Ω. Right: on a log scale the filter's Fourier tail falls below every power law, which keeps each piece quasi-local.

diagrams.caption: Equation eq:quasilocal-ce: truncating an operator to a ball traces out everything outside (the loop) and puts back the normalized identity there.

stages.title: Replicas trade information against energy
stages.physics: Take k copies of the ground state, each beside a maximally entangled pair on registers C and R, and keep one Schur–Weyl sector of the R registers: {{tn:al-prevector}}. Filter by an inverse power of an operator that interpolates as a small region changes sides; per copy, the log-norm of the filtered vector approaches a combination of entropies. Trees of matrix geometric means carry out the bookkeeping.
stages.delivers: The decrease of the log-norm bounds conditional mutual information from below, and the same states bound the energy spent. Projecting the target and C onto a pair moves the target's Schmidt index onto R, {{tn:al-pin}}, which gives the upper comparison. The gap gives the lower one, because low energy forces most copies into Ω.
stages.caption: As the number m of copies grows, the log-norm per copy of the filtered vector settles at a combination of entropies (dashed). Comparing this limit with the energy spent is what bounds the conditional mutual information.

diagrams.caption: Lemma lem:movement, eq:conditional-movement. Filtering a piece x of a pure state θ through the U side and then the P side loses norm at the rate η = I(x : F | U) = I(x : F | P).

stages.title: Scan a collar
stages.physics: Sweep the partition through a collar along a finite randomized schedule, so that each interaction term is rarely cut. Applied repeatedly, the two norm comparisons first improve the box exponent and then bound the information shared by the target X and the region beyond the collar, in the state {{tn:al-collar}} where the collar has been traced out.
stages.delivers: The mutual information between A∩T and the region beyond a collar of width n1−ε is at most C n1−ε, for templates T with O(n) boundary.
stages.caption: Five steps of the sweep as small multiples. The partition (orange) crosses the collar (grey) at a different position in each step, chosen by a randomized schedule, so each interaction term is cut in only a few steps.

stages.title: Amplify the information bound
stages.physics: Typical spectral subspaces give an operator that restores the target from an auxiliary reference. Localized products of the positive constraints suppress its excited part, and polar decomposition turns it into a unitary U′ acting only near the target: {{tn:al-restore}}. Because U′ never touches the reference e′ or the far region, the target ends up nearly independent of both.
stages.delivers: Widening the collar by a sublinear amount makes the leaked information smaller than any fixed inverse power of n.
stages.caption: Information leaked past the collar against its width, on a log scale. The scan leaves at most C n1−ε. Widening the collar by a sublinear amount drives the leak below every fixed inverse power of n.

stages.title: Arrange regions so the entropies cancel
stages.physics: Remove O(|∂A|) sites D and split the rest of A into two ordered families of regions. A collar separates each region from the outside and from the earlier regions of its family. Since the state is pure, {{tn:al-purity}}: the two marginals share their nonzero spectrum. Narrow strips and recursive repairs at point contacts make this work for arbitrary cuts, including domains with holes.
stages.delivers: Two applications of the entropy chain rule cancel the entropy of every region, leaving S(A) ≤ |D| log q plus summable errors. This is the area law.
stages.caption: The region A drawn cell by cell. A boundary layer D of O(|∂A|) sites is removed (solid squares), and the rest is cut into two ordered families of strips. In the entropy chain rule each strip's entropy is added once and removed once, leaving |D| log q plus summable errors.

routes.heading: How the PEPS is built
routes.intro: The construction distributes the ground state among parties, one for each dyadic square, until every site has its own party. Parties may act arbitrarily on what they hold, and each interacts with boundedly many others over its lifetime. Compressing the shared resources gives polynomial bonds, and routing the links places them on the original grid.

stages.title: Information fades with angular separation
stages.physics: Two regions separated by a buffer that tapers linearly toward finitely many points, and stays wider than a large multiple of log L, are almost independent. The proof adds cells one at a time using the two tile families of the area law. Gaussian filtering with the gap resets the cost after each annular step.
stages.delivers: Mutual information at most L−p. The owner of the buffer U can then split its share with an isometry V into a product, {{tn:peps-split}}, with error at most √I(T : E).
stages.caption: Two regions X and Y separated by a buffer that narrows linearly toward a point but never drops below a large multiple of log L (orange). Their mutual information is at most a fixed inverse power of L.

stages.title: Small patches with polynomial rank
stages.physics: Near a square of logarithmic size, the state lies almost entirely in an orthogonal sum of subspaces. Each is spanned by a few vectors inside a nested square, tensored with everything outside. The proof combines nested filters, the gap and the area law, and needs no sharp truncation at one fixed boundary.
stages.delivers: Total inside rank Σdj ≤ C Lc. An encoder supported on the hole records which cylinder and which inside vector in a small open register 𝒥: {{tn:peps-encode}}.
stages.caption: Left: nested squares around a square of side about log L. Right: the inside rank of each subspace in the orthogonal sum, as bars. Their total is polynomial in L, so the label fits in a small register.

stages.title: Local moves on frames
stages.physics: The elementary operations change which party owns a region, create or retire a party, and exchange registers between two copies of the state. A birth consumes and re-emits one normalized pair source, {{tn:peps-pair}}, whose T half goes to the new party; everything else is a private map.
stages.delivers: Each move has error of order L−30 at most, small enough to sum over the whole protocol.
stages.caption: The three elementary moves, each drawn before and after: a region passes from party a to party b; a party splits off a new party or retires; a register (orange) moves between two copies of the state.

diagrams.caption: Lemma lem:birth, read bottom to top. The owner of T and U splits with V, consumes s on T𝓑T, emits a fresh pair source |s⟩ whose T half belongs to the new party, and recombines with V†. Error at most L−30.
Lemma lem:small-rewrite: a small patch is re-encoded by M = KnewPm⋯P1Kold†, with error at most (m + rold)ε.

stages.title: A dyadic distribution protocol
stages.physics: One party starts with Ω. Ownership passes down a hierarchy of dyadic squares until each site has its own party. Extra copies of Ω supply the surrounding regions that each change of owner needs.
stages.delivers: Every party takes part in boundedly many operations with other parties, at two adjacent scales.
stages.caption: The hierarchy as small multiples, from one party to one party per site. The outlined square in each panel is a parent; its children (blue) are the parties it interacts with at the next scale.

stages.title: Compress the shared resources
stages.physics: The protocol uses pair resources of unbounded Schmidt rank. In the density calculation each source operator is replaced by a Gaussian sum of polynomially many product operators, exact on average: {{tn:peps-source}}. Bounded participation limits the coefficient cost, and a Gaussian second-moment bound controls the error.
stages.delivers: A trace-norm error independent of every private dimension, and an operator network with polynomial bonds on the party graph.

stages.title: Back to a vector on the grid
stages.physics: Fixing the input legs of the compressed operator to one product vector gives a ket network with the same bonds, {{tn:peps-column}}, and some such column is close to Ω. The links join parties at nearby dyadic scales. Routed along rows and columns, they cross each lattice edge a bounded number of times.
stages.delivers: A PEPS {{tn:peps-sheet}} on the original L×L grid with bond dimension at most C Lc and error at most 1/L.
stages.caption: The links between parents and children on an 8 × 8 grid, routed first along a row and then along a column. Stroke width counts the links that share each lattice edge, which sets the bond dimension there.

diagrams.caption: The result, as defined in the introduction: one tensor Av per site of the open L×L grid, bonds along grid edges, one physical leg per site, bond dimension at most C Lc.

stages.title: Models and conventions
stages.physics: Both proofs use the same definitions: Hamiltonians on finite lattice domains, possibly with holes; regional reduced states and their entropies; the equivalence of the global gap with an energy estimate; and an exact match between the PEPS of the papers, one tensor {{tn:peps-tensor}} per site, and the tensor networks of TNLean.
stages.delivers: Lean statements of both main theorems with no hypothesis the papers lack.
stages.caption: A finite domain Λ of the square lattice, with a hole and an irregular edge, and a region A (blue). The orange edges form ∂ΛA, the count that the area law bounds the entropy by.

glossary: S(A) = −Tr ρ<sub>A</sub> log ρ<sub>A</sub> for the reduced state of region A. It measures how entangled A is with the rest of the system.
I(B:C) = S(B) + S(C) − S(B∪C), the total correlation between B and C. Small I means B and C are nearly independent.
A buffer zone of chosen width around a region. The area-law proof shows that almost no information crosses a collar of slightly sublinear width.
The energy gap Δ of the full Hamiltonian above its unique ground state. No gap is assumed for any subregion.
A state built by contracting one tensor per site along the lattice edges. The bond dimension D is the size of each contracted index.
Many copies of the ground state taken together. The argument works in their symmetric subspace and then lets the number of copies grow.
